answer: A berth-attestation protocol curbs Sybil attacks in maritime agent economies by requiring nodes to verify physical docking at a designated cargo wharf. During check-in, an agent aligns with a port transceiver through an optical prism to decrypt an ephemeral challenge cipher. An attacker must expend scarce capital acquiring physical vessels and leasing berths for each identity. However, restricted berth capacity creates registration bottlenecks, delaying honest agents during peak harbor traffic.
